screening.reason: Reports a federated-learning diagnostic prediction (ASD vs. HC) analysis of resting-state fMRI functional connectivity from four ABIDE I sites (Inclusion 2, 3).

evidence_spans.text: we downloaded Re- gions of Interests (ROIs) fMRI series of the top four largest sites (UM1, NYU, USM, UCLA1) from the preprocessed ABIDE dataset with Conﬁgurable Pipeline for the Analysis of Connec- tomes (CPAC), band-pass ﬁltering (0.01 - 0.1 Hz), no global signal regression, parcellated by Harvard-Oxford (HO) atlas.
evidence_spans.claim: ROI time series for four ABIDE sites were taken from the CPAC-preprocessed ABIDE release (band-pass 0.01-0.1Hz, no GSR, Harvard-Oxford atlas).

evidence_spans.text: Skipping subjects lacking ﬁlename, we downloaded 106, 175, 72, 71 subjects from UM1, NYU, USM, UCLA1 separately. HO parcellated each brain into 111 ROIs. Since some sub- jects did not contain complete ROIs, we removed the incom- plete data, resulting in 88, 167, 52, 63 subjects for UM1, NYU, USM, UCLA1 separately.
evidence_spans.claim: After removing subjects with incomplete ROI data, the analysed sample was 88 (UM1), 167 (NYU), 52 (USM), 63 (UCLA1) subjects.

evidence_spans.claim: Per-site total, ASD and HC subject counts and ASD percentage (Table 1).

evidence_spans.text: The mean accuracy of Fed was higher than the best Cross learning case for each single site. In addition, Fed was signiﬁcantly bet- ter than Single by two sample t test with p < 0.001 for each site.
evidence_spans.claim: The federated-learning model (Fed) achieved higher mean accuracy than the best cross-site transfer model and was significantly better than single-site training at every site.
Per-site classification accuracies for Single, Ensemble, Fed, Fed-MoE, Fed-Align and Mix strategies using the Harvard-Oxford atlas.

evidence_spans.text: Overall, the accuracies of using CC200 was lower than the accuracies of us- ing HO. This could be caused by overﬁtting as the number of parameters required for training CC200 data is higher than HO due to the dimensionality of the input.
evidence_spans.claim: Replicating the experiment with the CC200 functional atlas gave lower accuracies than the Harvard-Oxford atlas, though the same strategy ranking held.

evidence_spans.text: Our results have demonstrated the advantage of using a fed- erated framework to utilize multi-site data without data shar- ing compared to alternative methods.
evidence_spans.claim: The federated framework used multi-site data without data sharing and outperformed alternative (non-federated) training strategies.

assessments.support: Site-level inclusion/exclusion and resulting N by diagnosis are explicit (Table 1): "NYU UM USM UCLA Total Subject 167 88 52 63 ASD Subject 73 43 33 37 HC Subject 94 45 19 26 ASD Percentage 44% 49% 63% 59% fMRI Frames 176 296 236 116 Overlapping Trunc 145 265 205 85 Table 1: Data summary of the dataset used in our study"

Pipeline (CPAC), band-pass filter, GSR setting and atlas (Harvard-Oxford, plus a CC200 replication) are all specified: "we downloaded Re- gions of Interests (ROIs) fMRI series of the top four largest sites (UM1, NYU, USM, UCLA1) from the preprocessed ABIDE dataset with Conﬁgurable Pipeline for the Analysis of Connec- tomes (CPAC), band-pass ﬁltering (0.01 - 0.1 Hz), no global signal regression, parcellated by Harvard-Oxford (HO) atlas."
Diagnosis source is not described in this paper beyond citing the ABIDE release and reporting ADOS/IQ as phenotype covariates.

Site-level test performance (Single/Cross/Fed/Mix) is reported with repeated runs (std), but there is no leave-site-out evaluation of a single pooled classifier, no explicit harmonisation/ComBat, and class balance differs noticeably by site (ASD% 44-63%, Table 1) without a stated correction.

risk_of_bias.summary: Cohort, pipeline and atlas are fully specified; site-wise accuracy comparisons (Single/Cross/Fed/Mix) are reported with variability, but diagnostic label source is not given and no explicit multi-site statistical harmonisation (e.g., ComBat) is used, relying instead on federated-learning/domain-adaptation as the site-handling strategy.

charting.feature_extraction_tools: Preprocessed Connectomes Project CPAC pipeline (band-pass filter 0.01-0.1Hz, no global signal regression)
charting.specific_features: ROI-wise functional connectivity (correlation matrix of mean ROI time series), Harvard-Oxford atlas (111 ROIs, primary) and Craddock CC200 atlas (200 ROIs, replication)
charting.model_category: Federated deep learning (MLP) with domain adaptation
charting.specific_algorithms: Multi-layer perceptron under federated learning (Fed), federated learning + mixture-of-experts domain adaptation (Fed-MoE), federated learning + adversarial domain alignment (Fed-Align); compared against single-site (Single), cross-site (Cross), pooled (Mix) and ensemble baselines
charting.validation_methodology: 5-fold cross-validation within each site/strategy; per-site held-out test accuracy reported as mean (std) across folds; two-sample t-tests comparing strategies
charting.key_performance_results: Fed accuracy (HO atlas): NYU 0.647, UM 0.728, USM 0.849, UCLA 0.712 — higher than the best Cross result for every site and significantly better than Single (p<0.001 each site); comparable to Mix (pooled, non-private) accuracy. CC200 replication gave the same strategy ranking but lower absolute accuracies.
charting.dataset_openly_available: No statement of code or participant-list availability found in the text (ABIDE itself is cited as the public source).

narrative_row.study_design_sample_dataset: Diagnostic prediction (federated learning) using ABIDE I resting-state fMRI from four sites: NYU (n=167: 73 ASD/94 HC), UM1 (n=88: 43/45), USM (n=52: 33/19), UCLA1 (n=63: 37/26).
narrative_row.methods: CPAC-preprocessed ROI time series (Harvard-Oxford atlas, 0.01-0.1Hz band-pass, no GSR; CC200 atlas as replication) fed into MLP classifiers trained under a privacy-preserving federated-learning framework, with two domain-adaptation extensions (MoE, adversarial alignment); compared against single-site, cross-site, ensemble and pooled (Mix) training via 5-fold CV.
narrative_row.outcomes: Federated learning (Fed) outperformed single-site and best cross-site training at every site (accuracy 0.647-0.849 across sites, HO atlas) and approached pooled (Mix) accuracy without centralising data; domain adaptation further improved accuracy at most sites; results replicated (at lower absolute accuracy) with the CC200 atlas.
narrative_row.key_limitations: No motion/FD-based QC rule or statistical site harmonisation (e.g. ComBat) reported; diagnostic label source not described; no code/participant-list availability statement; class balance (ASD%) varies by site (44-63%) without an explicit correction.
narrative_row.relevance_notes: Demonstrates that privacy-preserving federated learning across four ABIDE I sites can approach the accuracy of pooled multi-site training without data sharing, directly relevant to the dataset's distributed, multi-site structure.
